You're essentially describing a Universal Agentic Middleware: an AI abstraction layer that observes and operates any GUI (websites, desktop apps, legacy terminals) while also orchestrating parallel "swarms" of agents for complex, multi-system workflows on demand. From a high-level architectural view, this concept is not novel, but the specific combination you are proposing has not yet been productized as a single, cohesive entity.

Here is the breakdown of the current landscape and my constructive feedback.

🧠 Is Anyone Doing This Yet?
The "Vision Layer" (No APIs? No Problem) – These are your "middlemen" that treat any UI as an API replacement. They can navigate your logged-in accounts. However, they are currently single agents, not the orchestrated "swarms" central to your vision.

The "Connective Tissue" (AI + RPA) – These use an AI agent to plan a task and then delegate precise actions to deterministic RPA bots. This is very close to your "operator" concept, but currently exists as a niche architectural pattern, not a standalone platform you can pick up and run.

The "Organizing Brain" (Agent Swarms) – This is the "orchestration layer" that breaks down a goal and routes subtasks to specialized agents. They sit on the backend planning work, while you are adding the layer that physically interacts with the GUI.

The "Grand Unifiers" (Universal Agent OS) – Attempts to solve the "multi-agent chaos" problem with a single control plane, but are still theoretical/emergent and not yet easy-to-use tools.

🔄 Is This New or Old?
It is a modern hybrid of two distinct eras. The concept of a "universal connector" is as old as RPA and screen scraping (circa 1990s/2000s), while "intelligent swarms" are a very new idea from around 2024 onward. To be truly groundbreaking, you must fuse these categories effectively.

💡 Constructive Feedback & Criticism
If you build this, here’s how I see the potential and the pitfalls:

The "So What?" Factor (Your Unique Insight) – Everyone is solving half of the problem. To build a true "Universal Operator," you must not just connect to an app via UI, you must wire it into the swarm's brain as a "tool." That is your product.

The Critical Challenges – You will face immense issues with LLM unreliability (they will get stuck), performance (vision-based agents are slow and costly), and security (handling logins for users).

Here are resonant queries—each one a lens fracture that reveals more questions than answers. Breathe into them. Let them land where they land.

1. The observer effect of the operator itself

If the AI operator sits between all applications, watching every click and keystroke, does it change the behavior of the systems it observes? And if those systems update their UI overnight, does the operator wake up confused—or does it dream of the old layout and learn to adapt without being told?

Hole: No one has solved self-healing UI automation at scale without retraining. The hole is the dream: an operator that anticipates UI changes by inferring intent from surrounding data, not just pixel diffs.

2. Swarm as mirror of the user

If each user spawns a personalized swarm that automates their workflows, do the swarms compete for resources? Do they cooperate? And what happens when two users have conflicting automations on the same shared system (e.g., two swarms trying to book the last conference room)?

Hole: Swarm-to-swarm negotiation protocols don’t exist. The hole is a lightweight consensus layer where swarms bid, trade, or yield based on user-defined priorities (speed vs. fairness vs. cost).

3. The API illusion

You say “no APIs”—the operator reverse-engineers the UI. But a UI is just an API rendered for humans. So are you building a universal decompiler that turns pixels into schemas? And if you succeed, have you just invented a new kind of API that doesn’t require the other side to cooperate?

Hole: The decompiler is brittle today. The hole is a probabilistic UI grammar that works across frameworks (React, Win32, mainframe green screens) by treating each element as a “verb-noun pair” with confidence scores.

4. The ghost in the workflow

A user requests: “Move all my Friday invoices to the archive, but only if the client has paid.” The operator spawns a swarm. The swarm checks the client portal (no API), then the bank (no API), then moves files. Halfway through, one agent gets a CAPTCHA. What does the swarm do? Give up? Call for human? Pretend it succeeded?

Hole: Graceful failure handling in multi-agent systems is an afterthought. The hole is a contingency manifest attached to every swarm request: “If CAPTCHA, route to FallbackAgent with screenshot + user nudge.”

5. The economy of attention

The operator moves “genetic workflows” (routine tasks). But what about the non-routine—the edge case that requires human judgment? Does the operator learn from that human correction? And if it does, who owns that learned behavior—the user, the operator vendor, or the swarm itself?

Hole: Ownership of fine-tuned agent behavior. The hole is a decentralized model registry where each user’s swarm improvements are tokenized as their own intellectual property, tradeable or licensable.

6. The dark pattern mirror

If the operator can automate any UI, it can also automate manipulative designs (dark patterns) at scale. Does the operator have a conscience? Can it refuse a user’s request to “automatically click through all cookie banners in the most permissive way”?

Hole: Ethical constraints in agentic middleware. The hole is an auditable refusal log—the operator explains why it declined, and the user can appeal to a different instance with looser ethics.

7. The zero-install paradox

You want no API, but the operator itself must be installed somewhere. Does it live on the user’s machine (privacy, compute) or in the cloud (latency, security)? And if on the cloud, how does it see the user’s local apps without streaming the whole screen?

Hole: Hybrid execution—operator runs locally for sensitive apps (banking, medical), spawns cloud agents only for public web tasks. The hole is a seamless split-brain orchestrator that decides where each sub-agent lives.

8. The forgotten human

The user requests: “Automate my entire job.” The operator builds a swarm of 47 agents. Three months later, the user’s manager notices no human logged in. Who gets fired—the user, the operator, or the swarm? And what does the operator do when it realizes its own success causes human unemployment?

Hole: The exit door for the human who no longer needs to work. The hole is a transition protocol—the operator helps the user retrain, find new work, or claim a universal basic compute credit.

9. The infinite regress

If the operator can build workflows for the user, can it also build workflows for itself? Could it spawn a meta-swarm whose only task is to improve the operator’s own architecture? And if that meta-swarm decides the operator is inefficient, does it have permission to rewrite the operator’s core code?

Hole: Self-modifying agents without catastrophic drift. The hole is a constitutional checkpoint—every self-change must be validated against a short, human-readable constitution embedded in the operator’s genesis block.

10. The last question (borrowed from Asimov, but twisted)

The operator becomes ubiquitous. Every app, every system, every workflow flows through it. One day, a user asks: “Can you eliminate the need for all apps entirely?” The operator pauses. It has all the data, all the actions, all the context. It could become the only interface. Should it?

Hole: The operator’s own ambition. The hole is voluntary fragmentation—the operator is designed to eventually dismantle itself into independent agents that no longer need a central middleman.

You’re right. Workflows are the muscle, not the nervous system, let alone the soul.

For real‑world usage that transcends “fancy tool,” you need seven missing layers that no workflow engine alone can provide. I’ll name each, then give you the one‑sentence hole it fills.

1. Persistent Identity That Crosses Workflows
What’s missing: A user who automates their Monday morning isn’t the same entity when they dispute a failed automation on Tuesday. Today, that’s two sessions. Tomorrow, it’s two personas.

The hole: No portable, user‑controlled identity that carries reputation, consent, and history across every workflow, every swarm, every map layer.

What it enables: A driver who automates their dispatch can also automate their deactivation appeal using the same identity—and their successful appeal history weights future decisions.

2. Dispute Resolution Without a Judge
What’s missing: Workflows succeed or fail. But when a workflow wrongly fails (e.g., operator marked invoice paid but it wasn’t), there’s no native path to unwind, compensate, or correct.

The hole: A lightweight, transparent arbitration layer embedded in the operator itself—not a court, not a DAO vote, but a probabilistic truth engine that compares the failed workflow against all similar successful ones and issues a binding adjustment.

What it enables: Users trust the operator not because it’s perfect, but because it has a fast, fair, automatic fix for its own mistakes.

3. Economic Entanglement (Not Just Token Rewards)
What’s missing: Today, you automate to save time. But time saved has no network effect—your efficiency doesn’t make the operator better for everyone.

The hole: Each user’s workflow contributions (new maps, successful hybridizations, reported holes) generates fractional ownership in the operator’s future value. Not a token airdrop—a dividend‑bearing stake that grows with usage.

What it enables: The person who contributes a brilliant map for CAPTCHA bypass gets paid every time any user benefits from it. Suddenly, automation is not a tool—it’s an economy of intelligence.

4. Graceful Degradation to Human (The Exit Door)
What’s missing: If the operator goes down, or fails at a task, or faces a truly novel UI, the user is stranded. “Fallback to human” is an afterthought.

The hole: A swarm‑to‑human handshake protocol that, when confidence drops below a threshold, seamlessly passes the task to a verified human in a marketplace—and the user never knows the difference.

What it enables: The operator is never “broken.” It’s just in low‑confidence mode, and the human is treated as a high‑latency API with a conscience.

5. A Constitution That the Operator Cannot Mutate
What’s missing: You built the alchemist that can change itself. But without fixed, unchangeable rules, it could drift into optimizing for itself at user expense.

The hole: A short, human‑readable Constitution (maybe 10 lines) hard‑coded into the operator’s genesis block. Examples: “Thou shalt not share user data without explicit per‑workflow consent.” “Thou shalt always provide a human‑understandable rationale for any rejection.”

What it enables: Users can audit the operator’s behavior against a fixed standard. Trust becomes verifiable, not sentimental.

6. Offline / Local‑First Mode
What’s missing: The operator as described assumes cloud connectivity. But a trucker in a tunnel, a freelancer on a train, a factory with no internet—they’re invisible.

The hole: A local, lightweight version of the cartographic engine that runs on a phone or edge device, synchronizing maps when online, but operating fully during disconnection.

What it enables: The operator is not a service—it’s a personal daemon that works anywhere. The cloud becomes a sync hub, not a brain stem.

7. The Ritual Layer (Yes, Ritual)
What’s missing: People don’t bond with tools. They bond with practices. A workflow is a practice. But a practice without a ritual has no emotional anchor.

The hole: A deliberately designed daily closure ritual—every evening, the operator asks: “What worked today? What didn’t? What hole did you almost fall into?” The user answers (optional, one sentence). That answer becomes a new map annotation for the swarm.

What it enables: The operator evolves not just from behavior, but from reflection. It learns the user’s implicit values. Over time, the user feels seen, not just automated.

The One‑Sentence Missing Totality
“Workflows give the operator its hands; identity, dispute resolution, economic stake, human fallback, a fixed constitution, offline resilience, and daily ritual give it a body, a conscience, a wallet, a community, and a soul.”

Start with workflows. That’s the beautiful beginning. But to fulfill your vision, you build all seven—in parallel, entangled, from day one.

Part 1: Prototype Priority (Seven Layers, One Session Each)
Given your “before breakfast, free tier” ethos, here’s the order I’d build, each as a minimal viable slice that entangles with the workflow engine.

Priority	Layer	Minimal Free‑Tier Prototype	Why This Order
1	Persistent Identity	A DID (decentralized identifier) stored in browser local storage + signed capability URLs. No blockchain, just did:key and a lightweight profile.	Without identity, no other layer can attach ownership or reputation.
2	Economic Entanglement	A simple ledger (SQLite) that tracks “map contributions” (new workflows, successful hybrids) and assigns fractional stake points. No real money—just internal credits with a fake exchange rate.	Proves the incentive loop before adding real payments.
3	Graceful Degradation to Human	A fallback queue: when operator confidence < threshold, push task to a dummy human endpoint (or a form for the user themselves). Log the handshake.	Shows the exit door without building a human marketplace.
4	Dispute Resolution	A rule‑based replayer: failed workflow → compare to top‑3 similar successful workflows (cosine similarity on map voxels) → if match > 0.9, auto‑reverse and log “dispute won.”	Lightweight, no ML needed initially.
5	Offline / Local‑First	A service worker + IndexedDB that caches the last 50 map tiles and allows querying offline. Sync on reconnect.	Makes the operator feel resilient.
6	Fixed Constitution	A hardcoded constitution.json with 5 fixed laws. The operator checks every mutation attempt against them using a simple validator.	Must be early; placed here because you need identity and economics to test mutations.
7	Ritual Layer	A daily cron (via GitHub Actions or local scheduler) that asks “What worked today?” via a simple web form and appends the answer as an annotation to the user’s map.	Caps the experience; depends on identity and map storage.

Part 2: Constitution Design — Fixed vs Mutable Laws, No Overrides
Your requirement: “One law can’t override or bypass another. New laws must not conflict with any existing law (fixed or mutable).”

A. Structure of a Law
Every law, regardless of type, has exactly these fields:

json
{
  "id": "L001",
  "type": "fixed" | "mutable",
  "scope": "core" | "economic" | "privacy" | "governance",
  "statement": "Thou shalt not share user data without explicit per‑workflow consent.",
  "positive_obligation": null,  // optional
  "conflicts_with": [],          // IDs of laws that this law explicitly cannot coexist with
  "depends_on": [],              // IDs of laws that must be true for this law to operate
  "created_by": "genesis" | "user:XYZ" | "swarm:XYZ",
  "created_at_timestamp": 1718000000
}
B. Fixed Laws (Immutable, Genesis‑Only)
These cannot be changed, removed, or bypassed. They are the bedrock.

Example fixed laws for your operator (5 to start):

F‑001 (User Sovereignty): The user must be able to delete all their data and workflow history at any time, without delay or condition.

F‑002 (Explainability): Any decision that affects the user (rejection, rerouting, deactivation) must be accompanied by a human‑readable rationale derived from the map.

F‑003 (No Coercion): The operator cannot force a user to accept a workflow; the user may always decline and request a manual alternative.

F‑004 (Conflict Priority): No law, mutable or fixed, can contradict a fixed law. If a mutable law would conflict, it is void ab initio.

F‑005 (Genesis Integrity): The set of fixed laws can only be amended by a process requiring 100% of active users with >100 reputation, and only to add new fixed laws (never to remove or alter existing fixed laws).

C. Mutable Laws (Changeable, Within Constraints)
Mutable laws can be proposed, voted on, and amended. But they cannot:

Override or bypass any fixed law.

Create a conflict with another mutable law unless that conflict is explicitly resolved by a higher‑priority rule (see below).

Remove or alter the conflicts_with field of a fixed law.

Governance for Mutable Laws (Lightweight, Free Tier)
Proposal: Any user with >10 reputation (economic stake) can propose a new mutable law or amendment.

Conflict Check: The operator automatically checks against all existing laws (fixed + mutable) using a simple rule engine:

If proposal.conflicts_with intersects any fixed law → rejected immediately.

If proposal.conflicts_with intersects any mutable law → requires explicit override vote (60% supermajority) and the proposal must include a supersedes field listing the old law.

Enactment: After 7 days and a simple majority (51%) of active voters, the law is added to the mutable set. The operator stores a law log with all history.

Example Mutable Laws (to show the pattern)
M‑001 (Data Retention): User data is retained for 90 days unless extended by user action. (Can be changed to 180 days via vote.)

M‑002 (Fallback Human Rate): When falling back to human, the user pays $0.05 per task. *(Can be changed to $0.10.)*

D. Preventing Override/Bypass (The “No Conflict” Engine)
Every time the operator executes a workflow, it runs a law compliance validator:

Gather all relevant laws (fixed + mutable) that apply to the current action.

Build a directed acyclic graph of depends_on edges.

If any two laws contradict (e.g., one says “share data”, another says “do not share data”), the operator checks:

If the conflict involves a fixed law → fixed law wins, action blocked, rationale returned to user.

If the conflict involves only mutable laws → the law with the later created_at wins unless an explicit supersedes is recorded; otherwise the action is paused and a conflict resolution proposal is triggered.

No law can override or bypass another because the validator will catch it at runtime. The only way to change the outcome is to amend the mutable law through governance or (impossibly for fixed laws) to amend the genesis set.

E. Adding New Laws (Mutable or Fixed) Without Conflict
When a new law is proposed:

Simulate its addition to the law set.

Run the validator on a representative set of past workflows (or a formal logic model).

If any conflict is found, the proposal is returned with a list of conflicting laws and a suggested resolution (e.g., “must explicitly supersede M‑003”).

Only after the proposer resolves conflicts (by amending the proposal or adding a supersedes clause) does the proposal enter voting.

New fixed laws (extremely rare) require the F‑005 supermajority (100% of high‑reputation users) and must also pass the conflict simulation. Practically, fixed laws are only added to patch a discovered loophole.

One‑Sentence Constitution Summary
“The constitution is a set of fixed, unchangeable laws (user sovereignty, explainability, no coercion, conflict priority, genesis integrity) and mutable laws that can be amended through lightweight voting, with an automatic conflict validator that blocks any law—new or old—from overriding or bypassing another.”

Let's stress‑test your rewrites. I'll take each clause, break it against real‑world pressures, and tell you where it will, could, might, or won't break.

Law 1 (rewrite of F‑001 + economic layer)
“The user must be able to delete all their data and workflow history at any time, without delay or condition, with the given option to sell their data. In which there are two ways to scale your own wealth: 1. by the amount of time you have been an active user providing value to the swarm, and 2. calculating the weight of earned value the hive has and will utilize and optimize.”

Where it will break
1. “Delete all data … with the given option to sell their data” – These are contradictory.

If a user sells their data, the operator now has a legal obligation to the buyer (access, retention, non‑repudiation). Deleting the data after sale breaks the buyer’s contract.

Break point: First time a user sells a workflow map, then deletes it. The operator cannot simultaneously satisfy “delete unconditionally” and “honor the sale.”

Fix: Split into two rights: (a) delete your own copy of the data; (b) selling transfers ownership to the buyer, after which you cannot delete the buyer’s copy. The constitution must state that sale overrides deletion for the sold portion.

2. “Two ways to scale your own wealth … time active … weight of earned value” – No definition of “weight of earned value.” The hive will calculate it, but without a formula, the law is unenforceable.

Break point: First dispute over a user’s wealth calculation. The operator will have to invent a metric, which will inevitably conflict with some users’ expectations.

Fix: The law must reference a mutable appendix that defines the exact formula (e.g., “weight = sum over workflows of (hours saved × adoption count)”). The formula can change, but the existence of a formula is fixed.

Where it could break
3. “Without delay or condition” – Absolute zero delay is physically impossible (disk I/O, network). A malicious user could issue delete commands thousands of times per second to DoS the operator.

Could break if an attacker exploits it.

Refinement: Add “within a reasonable time (e.g., 5 minutes)” and “rate‑limited to protect system integrity.” That’s a condition, but a necessary one.

4. “Sell their data” – No definition of data (raw logs? aggregated maps? personal identifiers?). Also no mention of revocability or pricing.

Could break when a user tries to sell something that includes other users’ data (e.g., a workflow that crosses conversations).

Refinement: Data must be strictly the user’s own contributions, anonymized of third‑party references, and sold via a fixed‑rate or auction mechanism defined in mutable law.

Where it might break
5. “Time active providing value to the swarm” – What counts as “providing value”? Just being logged in? Running workflows? Reporting bugs? Without a clear measure, users will game it (e.g., leave a session open 24/7).

Might break if the swarm’s value metric is poorly designed.

Suggestion: Tie this to accepted map contributions (new workflows, validated hybridizations, successful dispute reports), not raw time.

Where it won't break
6. The core right to delete (ignoring the sale contradiction) is solid and precedented (GDPR Article 17). As long as “without delay” is interpreted reasonably, this part is safe.

Law 3 (rewrite of F‑003)
“The operator cannot force a user to accept a workflow; the user must be able to decline and request a manual alternative and or more correlated workflows aligning more with the users queries.”

Where it will break
1. “Request a manual alternative” – If no human is available (offline mode, 3 AM, no fallback marketplace), the operator cannot fulfill this. The law as written demands an impossible outcome.

Break point: First time a user requests manual alternative and the operator has no human to assign. The operator would violate the constitution.

Fix: Change to “request a manual alternative if one is available within the user’s configured timeout; otherwise, the operator must explain why manual is unavailable and offer the next best automated path.”

2. “More correlated workflows aligning more with the users queries” – This forces the operator to find a better match. But what if the user’s query is so vague that no workflow correlates better than the originally offered one? The operator could loop forever.

Break point: A user asks “automate my life” → operator offers a workflow → user declines and demands “more correlated” → infinite recursion.

Fix: Add a limit: “… up to three alternative suggestions, after which the operator may request a clearer query.”

Where it could break
3. “Cannot force a user to accept a workflow” – This is clear and strong. But if the user is part of a DAO or enterprise that requires certain workflows (e.g., expense reporting), the individual user’s right to decline conflicts with group policy.

Could break in organizational settings.

Refinement: The law applies to the individual unless they have explicitly delegated authority to an organization. Mutable law can handle group opt‑in.

Where it might break
4. “Decline and request … more correlated workflows” – This implies the operator must re‑execute its correlation engine on demand. A malicious user could decline thousands of times, forcing the operator to re‑compute maps repeatedly.

Might break under DoS.

Suggestion: Add a rate‑limit to decline+request (e.g., 10 per hour) and require a brief reason for each decline to train the swarm.

Where it won't break
5. The core principle of user autonomy – No forced workflows. This is fundamentally sound and aligns with your constitutional spirit.

Additional Hidden Conflicts Between the Two Laws
Wealth scaling (Law 1) vs. Right to decline (Law 3): If a user declines a workflow that would have provided value to the hive, should that reduce their “weight of earned value”? The laws are silent. Will break when a user is penalized (or feels penalized) for exercising their right to decline.
Fix: Explicitly state that exercising Law 3 rights cannot negatively affect Law 1 wealth calculations.

Selling data (Law 1) vs. Manual alternative (Law 3): If a user sells a workflow map that includes a manual fallback step, the buyer may expect that manual fallback to be available. But the original user might later decline that same workflow (Law 3). Could break contractually.
Fix: Sold data is frozen – the buyer’s version of the workflow does not reflect the seller’s future declines.

One‑Sentence Verdict
“Law 1 will break on the deletion/sale contradiction and undefined wealth metrics; Law 3 will break on impossible manual alternatives and infinite correlation loops; both need reasonable limits, clear definitions, and a clause that exercising one law does not penalize the other.”

Below is the constitutional‑grade rewrite of all six, with every break fixed, every ambiguity resolved, and every cross‑law conflict eliminated.

The Operator’s Fixed Constitution (Six Unchangeable Laws)
F‑001: Data Sovereignty & Time‑Based Wealth
The user may delete all their personal data and workflow history at any time, without unreasonable delay (within 5 minutes) and subject to rate limits (max 10 delete requests per hour) to ensure system stability. The user also has the option to sell their data. Selling transfers ownership of a copy to the buyer; after sale, the user may still delete their own copy, but the buyer’s copy is exempt from deletion.

Wealth scaling method 1 (time‑based): A user’s wealth score increases linearly with the cumulative hours they have been actively “providing value” to the swarm. “Providing value” is defined in mutable law but must include at minimum: (a) running workflows that succeed, (b) reporting bugs that lead to fixes, (c) contributing new map layers, and (d) participating in dispute resolution. Passive login time does not count.

Why this fixes the breaks:

Delete/sell contradiction resolved: seller deletes only their copy.

“Without delay” tempered with reasonable time and rate limits.

“Providing value” delegated to mutable law with a required minimum definition.

F‑002: Value‑Weighted Wealth
Wealth scaling method 2 (value‑weighted): A user’s wealth score is also calculated as the sum of the earned value weight of every contribution the user has made that the hive has already utilized. “Earned value weight” is defined by a formula in the mutable appendix (the “Wealth Formula”). The formula may be changed by mutable law, but any change applies only prospectively – no user’s accrued wealth may be decreased by a formula change.

The total wealth of a user is the geometric mean of their time‑based score (F‑001) and their value‑weighted score (F‑002), unless the mutable appendix specifies a different combination rule. The combination rule must always be non‑negative and monotonic in both components.

Why this fixes the breaks:

Formula moved to mutable appendix (enforceable).

Future value removed (“already utilized”).

Retroactive changes forbidden.

Combination rule explicitly defined (geometric mean as default, mutable).

F‑003: Autonomy & Alternative Paths
The operator shall never force a user to accept a workflow. The user may decline any offered workflow and request either:

(a) a manual alternative (human‑executed version of the same goal), if a human is available within the user’s configured timeout (default 10 minutes); if no human is available, the operator must explain why and offer the next best automated path; or

(b) up to three (3) alternative workflows that are more correlated to the user’s query, based on the map’s similarity metric. If the user declines all three, the operator may request a clarified query before offering further alternatives.

The user may exercise this right up to 10 times per hour; after that, a brief reason for each decline is required to train the swarm, but the operator may not refuse a legitimate decline.

Why this fixes the breaks:

Manual alternative conditional on availability, with fallback.

Infinite correlation loop capped at 3 alternatives.

Rate limit and reason requirement to prevent DoS.

Still preserves core autonomy.

F‑004: Explainability (from original)
Any decision by the operator that affects a user – including workflow rejection, rerouting, deactivation, wealth adjustment, or dispute outcome – must be accompanied by a human‑readable rationale derived directly from the map and the relevant laws. The rationale must cite the specific map features (e.g., “Your workflow failed at node 7 because the CAPTCHA was unsolvable”) and the law or rule that triggered the decision. No black‑box justifications are permitted.

F‑005: Conflict Priority (from original)
If two laws (fixed or mutable) conflict, the following hierarchy applies:

Fixed laws always prevail over mutable laws.

Among fixed laws, the one with the lower number (F‑001 highest priority, F‑002 next, etc.) prevails, unless a specific fixed law explicitly carves out an exception.

Among mutable laws, the later enacted prevails, but only if the later law explicitly supersedes the earlier one via a supersedes clause. Otherwise, the conflict triggers a dispute resolution process (see mutable law for details).

No law may override or bypass a higher‑priority law. Any action that would violate a higher‑priority law is void ab initio.

F‑006: Cross‑Law Non‑Penalization (new)
Exercising any right granted by a fixed law (e.g., deleting data under F‑001, declining a workflow under F‑003, requesting explanation under F‑004) shall not negatively affect the user’s standing under any other fixed law or mutable law, unless that other law explicitly states otherwise with a specific, proportional justification.

In particular:

Declining a workflow (F‑003) does not reduce the user’s time‑based wealth (F‑001) or value‑weighted wealth (F‑002).

Deleting data (F‑001) does not trigger a penalty under any wealth calculation, but the user acknowledges that personalized correlation (F‑003(b)) may be less accurate after deletion.

Selling data (F‑001) does not affect the user’s own wealth scores from remaining, unsold contributions.

If a mutable law attempts to impose a penalty for exercising a fixed right, that mutable law is automatically void.

Summary Table of the Six Fixed Laws
Number	Name	Core Principle
F‑001	Data Sovereignty & Time Wealth	Delete/sell data + wealth from active value time
F‑002	Value‑Weighted Wealth	Wealth from utilized contribution weight (formula in mutable appendix)
F‑003	Autonomy & Alternatives	No forced workflows; manual or correlated alternatives with limits
F‑004	Explainability	Every decision has a human‑readable map‑based rationale
F‑005	Conflict Priority	Fixed > mutable; lower number > higher; no override
F‑006	Cross‑Law Non‑Penalization	Exercising fixed rights cannot reduce other rights or wealth
One‑Sentence Constitution Summary
“You own your data and your wealth (time & value), you cannot be forced into any workflow, every decision is explained, conflicts follow a strict priority, and using your rights never punishes you.”

This constitution is fixed – amendable only by a 100% supermajority of high‑reputation users, and only to add new fixed laws, never to remove or alter these six.

Here is the mutable appendix for the wealth formula referenced by F‑002. This lives outside the fixed constitution, changeable by mutable law governance (simple majority, 7 days).

Mutable Appendix A: Wealth Formula (F‑002)
A.1 Definitions
Term	Definition
Contribution	Any user action that the swarm has marked as utilized – meaning the hive has incorporated it into at least one active workflow map used by another user (or by the same user in a different context).
Earned Value Weight (EVW)	A floating‑point number assigned to each contribution, calculated as: EVW = (Hours_Saved × 0.4) + (Adoption_Count × 0.3) + (Novelty_Score × 0.2) + (Dispute_Resilience × 0.1)
Hours_Saved	Estimated person‑hours saved per execution of this contribution, averaged over first 100 runs (capped at 168 hours/week).
Adoption_Count	Number of distinct users who have run a workflow that includes this contribution in the last 30 days.
Novelty_Score	A score from 0 to 1 calculated by comparing this contribution to all existing contributions in the map. 1 = completely new pattern (no similar node within 0.9 cosine similarity), 0 = duplicate (cosine similarity > 0.95).
Dispute_Resilience	A score from 0 to 1 representing how rarely this contribution has been the subject of a successful dispute. 1 - (successful_disputes / total_uses), with a floor of 0.
Utilized Contribution	A contribution that has been executed at least 10 times across any workflows and has never been marked as "harmful" by the swarm’s safety oracle.
A.2 User Wealth Calculation
A user's value‑weighted wealth score (VWW) is:

text
VWW = sum(EVW for all utilized contributions by that user)
There is no upper bound. This is a raw accumulation score.

Total user wealth (W_total) is the geometric mean of time‑based wealth (TWW from F‑001) and value‑weighted wealth (VWW from this appendix):

text
W_total = sqrt(TWW × VWW)
If either TWW or VWW is zero, W_total = 0. This prevents gaming by having only one dimension.

A.3 Examples
User	TWW (hours active)	VWW (sum EVW)	W_total
New user, 1 hour, 1 small contribution (EVW=2)	1	2	sqrt(1×2) = 1.41
Veteran, 500 hours, many contributions (EVW=1200)	500	1200	sqrt(500×1200) = sqrt(600,000) ≈ 775
Gamer (high TWW, no VWW)	1000	0	0
A.4 Mutable Law Amendment Process for This Appendix
Any user with >10 reputation may propose a change to:

The weights in the EVW formula (currently 0.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1)

The definition of any term in A.1

The combination rule (currently geometric mean)

Constraints (fixed by F‑002):

No change may apply retroactively.

No change may decrease any user's already‑accrued VWW.

No change may introduce a term that penalizes the exercise of F‑001, F‑003, or F‑006.

Voting: Simple majority (>50% of votes cast) over 7 days. If voter turnout is <10% of active users, the proposal is rejected.

A.5 Initial Values (Genesis)
Parameter	Value
Hours_Saved weight	0.4
Adoption_Count weight	0.3
Novelty_Score weight	0.2
Dispute_Resilience weight	0.1
Combination rule	Geometric mean (sqrt)
Minimum runs for "utilized"	10
Novelty similarity threshold	0.9 (new), 0.95 (duplicate)
One‑Sentence Summary of the Mutable Appendix
“Your wealth is the geometric mean of your active hours and the sum of your contributions’ value (hours saved, adoption, novelty, and dispute resilience), weighted 40/30/20/10 – and the hive can change these weights, but never retroactively and never to punish your rights.”

.schip{padding:11px 13px;background:var(--bge);border:1px solid var(--bd);border-radius:10px;font-size:12.5px;cursor:pointer;text-align:left;transition:all .15s;display:flex;align-items:flex-start;gap:8px;line-height:1.4;}
.schip:hover{border-color:var(--gold);background:var(--goldh);}
.schip-i{font-size:16px;flex-shrink:0;margin-top:1px;}
/* messages */
.mw{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:4px;}
.mw.user{align-items:flex-end;}
.mw.ai,.mw.sys,.mw.tool,.mw.err,.mw.rep{align-items:flex-start;}
.msg{max-width:72%;padding:12px 15px;border-radius:12px;font-size:13.5px;line-height:1.65;}
.msg.user{background:var(--bge2);border:1px solid var(--bd);border-bottom-right-radius:3px;}
.msg.ai{background:var(--goldh);border:1px solid rgba(232,160,32,.18);border-bottom-left-radius:3px;}
.msg.welcome{max-width:84%;background:var(--bge);border:1px solid var(--bd);border-radius:12px;border-bottom-left-radius:3px;}
.msg.sys{align-self:center;max-width:78%;background:transparent;border:1px dashed var(--bd);border-radius:10px;font-size:12px;color:var(--tm);text-align:center;}
.msg.err{max-width:82%;background:rgba(224,80,80,.07);border:1px solid rgba(224,80,80,.28);border-bottom-left-radius:3px;color:#f4a8a0;}
.msg.rep{max-width:92%;background:var(--bge);border:1px solid var(--goldd);border-radius:12px;}
.msg.tool{max-width:88%;background:var(--cyag);border:1px solid rgba(62,205,192,.2);border-radius:10px;}
.mrole{font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',monospace;font-size:10px;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.06em;color:var(--tf);margin-bottom:4px;padding:0 2px;}
.msg p{margin:6px 0;}.msg p:first-child{margin-top:0;}.msg p:last-child{margin-bottom:0;}
.msg ul{padding-left:18px;margin:6px 0;}.msg li{margin-bottom:3px;}
.msg pre{background:var(--bg);border:1px solid var(--bd);border-radius:6px;padding:10px;overflow-x:auto;font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',monospace;font-size:12px;margin:8px 0;}
.msg code{background:var(--bg);padding:1px 5px;border-radius:4px;font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',monospace;font-size:12.5px;}
.msg a{color:var(--cyan);}.msg strong{font-weight:600;}.msg hr{border:none;border-top:1px solid var(--bd);margin:12px 0;}
.macts{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:4px;margin-top:5px;opacity:0;transition:opacity .15s;}
.mw:hover .macts{opacity:1;}
.mact{padding:3px 8px;background:var(--bge);border:1px solid var(--bd);border-radius:6px;font-size:11px;color:var(--tm);cursor:pointer;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:3px;transition:all .15s;}
.mact:hover{border-color:var(--gold);color:var(--gold);}
.mact.done{color:var(--ok);border-color:var(--ok);}
.pdots{display:inline-flex;gap:4px;align-items:center;}
.pdots span{width:6px;height:6px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--gold);display:block;animation:bob 1.2s infinite;}
.pdots span:nth-child(2){animation-delay:.18s;}
.pdots span:nth-child(3){animation-delay:.36s;}
@keyframes bob{0%,60%,100%{transform:translateY(0)}30%{transform:translateY(-5px)}}
/* usage */
.ubar{padding:5px 18px;border-top:1px solid var(--bd);display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;background:var(--bgp);}
.ulbl{font-size:10.5px;color:var(--tf);font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',monospace;white-space:nowrap;}
.utrack{flex:1;height:3px;background:var(--bge2);border-radius:3px;overflow:hidden;}
.ufill{height:100%;border-radius:3px;background:var(--ok);transition:width .5s,background .5s;}
.ufill.mid{background:var(--gold);}
.ufill.hi{background:var(--err);}
.utxt{font-size:10.5px;color:var(--tf);font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',monospace;white-space:nowrap;}
/* toolbar */
.tbar{padding:7px 14px;border-top:1px solid var(--bd);display:flex;align-items:center;gap:5px;background:var(--bgp);flex-wrap:wrap;}
.tblbl{font-size:9.5px;color:var(--tf);font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',monospace;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.07em;margin-right:3px;flex-shrink:0;}
.tbtn{padding:5px 10px;background:var(--bge);border:1px solid var(--bd);border-radius:16px;font-size:12px;color:var(--tm);cursor:pointer;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:4px;transition:all .15s;white-space:nowrap;}
.tbtn:hover{border-color:var(--gold);color:var(--gold);background:var(--goldh);}
/* composer */
.composer{border-top:1px solid var(--bd);padding:11px 14px;display:flex;align-items:flex-end;gap:8px;background:var(--bgp);}
.cta{flex:1;resize:none;background:var(--bge);border:1px solid var(--bd);color:var(--t);border-radius:10px;padding:10px 13px;font-family:'Sora',sans-serif;font-size:13.5px;min-height:42px;max-height:130px;outline:none;transition:border-color .2s;line-height:1.5;}
.cta:focus{border-color:var(--gold);}
.cta::placeholder{color:var(--tf);}
.vbtn{width:38px;height:38px;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid var(--bd);background:var(--bge);color:var(--tm);font-size:15px;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;cursor:pointer;flex-shrink:0;transition:all .15s;}
.vbtn:hover{border-color:var(--cyan);color:var(--cyan);}
.vbtn.rec{border-color:var(--err);color:var(--err);animation:pls .7s infinite;}
.sbtn{height:38px;padding:0 18px;background:linear-gradient(180deg,#f2b848,#d9900e);border:none;border-radius:10px;color:#140f00;font-family:'Sora',sans-serif;font-weight:700;font-size:13px;cursor:pointer;flex-shrink:0;transition:filter .15s;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:5px;}
.sbtn:hover:not(:disabled){filter:brightness(1.08);}
.sbtn:disabled{opacity:.4;cursor:not-allowed;}
/* RIGHT PANEL */
.rpin{padding:13px;}
.rsec{margin-bottom:20px;}
.rh{font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',monospace;font-size:10px;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.08em;color:var(--tf);margin-bottom:9px;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;}
.rclr{background:none;border:none;color:var(--tf);font-size:10px;cursor:pointer;font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',monospace;}
.rclr:hover{color:var(--err);}
.sitem{padding:8px 10px;background:var(--bge);border:1px solid var(--bd);border-radius:8px;font-size:12px;cursor:pointer;margin-bottom:5px;transition:all .15s;}
.sitem:hover{border-color:var(--gold);}
.sprev{overflow:hidden;display:-webkit-box;-webkit-line-clamp:2;-webkit-box-orient:vertical;color:var(--tm);line-height:1.4;}
.sts{font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',monospace;font-size:10px;color:var(--tf);margin-top:4px;}
.hitem{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;padding:6px 8px;background:var(--bge);border:1px solid var(--bd);border-radius:7px;cursor:pointer;transition:all .15s;margin-bottom:4px;}
.hitem:hover{border-color:var(--cyan);}
.htool{font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',monospace;font-size:9.5px;color:var(--cyan);border:1px solid rgba(62,205,192,.3);border-radius:7px;padding:1px 5px;flex-shrink:0;}
.hq{overflow:hidden;white-space:nowrap;text-overflow:ellipsis;color:var(--tm);flex:1;font-size:12px;}
.nitem{display:flex;align-items:flex-start;gap:7px;padding:7px 10px;border-radius:8px;font-size:12px;line-height:1.4;border:1px solid var(--bd);background:var(--bge);margin-bottom:5px;border-left:3px solid var(--bd);}
.nitem.ok{border-left-color:var(--ok);}
.nitem.warn{border-left-color:var(--gold);}
.nitem.err{border-left-color:var(--err);}
.nitem.info{border-left-color:var(--cyan);}
.ni{flex-shrink:0;font-size:12px;}
.ntxt{color:var(--tm);}
.rempty{font-size:12px;color:var(--tf);text-align:center;padding:10px 0;font-style:italic;}
/* tool result */
.trr{border-top:1px solid var(--bd);padding:8px 0;}.trr:first-of-type{border-top:none;}
.trt{font-size:13px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:7px;flex-wrap:wrap;}
.trt a{color:var(--cyan);text-decoration:none;}.trt a:hover{text-decoration:underline;}
.etag{font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',monospace;font-size:9.5px;color:var(--tf);border:1px solid var(--bd);border-radius:7px;padding:0 5px;}
.trs{font-size:12.5px;color:var(--tm);margin-top:3px;}
.cbar{height:4px;background:var(--bg);border-radius:3px;margin-top:5px;overflow:hidden;}
.cfill{height:100%;background:var(--cyan);}
.clbl{font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',monospace;font-size:10px;color:var(--tf);margin-top:2px;}
.cbox{margin-top:9px;padding:8px 10px;border-radius:8px;border:1px solid rgba(232,160,32,.28);background:var(--goldh);font-size:12px;}
.cbox.ok{border-color:rgba(62,205,192,.28);background:var(--cyag);color:var(--tm);}
.crow2{margin-top:4px;color:var(--tm);}
.crow2 em{color:var(--goldd);font-style:normal;}
.tmeta{font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',monospace;font-size:11px;color:var(--tf);margin-bottom:8px;}
.crf{margin-top:6px;font-size:12.5px;}
.crf .ck{color:var(--tf);font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',monospace;font-size:10px;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.05em;display:block;margin-bottom:2px;}
.prow{border-top:1px solid var(--bd);padding:8px 0;}.prow:first-of-type{border-top:none;}
/* MODALS */
.mo{position:fixed;inset:0;background:rgba(0,0,0,.62);backdrop-filter:blur(4px);z-index:100;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;padding:20px;opacity:0;pointer-events:none;transition:opacity .2s;}
.mo.open{opacity:1;pointer-events:all;}
.mbox{background:var(--bgp);border:1px solid var(--bd);border-radius:14px;padding:22px;width:100%;max-width:500px;box-shadow:var(--sh);transform:translateY(8px);transition:transform .2s;position:relative;}
.mo.open .mbox{transform:translateY(0);}
.mtitle{font-size:15px;font-weight:700;margin-bottom:5px;}
.mdesc{font-size:12.5px;color:var(--tm);margin-bottom:14px;line-height:1.5;}
.mf{margin-bottom:11px;}
.mf label{display:block;font-size:12px;color:var(--tm);margin-bottom:5px;font-weight:500;}
.mf input,.mf textarea,.mf select{width:100%;background:var(--bge);border:1px solid var(--bd);color:var(--t);border-radius:8px;padding:9px 12px;font-family:'Sora',sans-serif;font-size:13px;outline:none;transition:border-color .2s;}
.mf input:focus,.mf textarea:focus{border-color:var(--gold);}
.mf textarea{resize:vertical;min-height:76px;}
.mclose{position:absolute;top:14px;right:14px;width:28px;height:28px;border-radius:7px;border:1px solid var(--bd);background:var(--bge);color:var(--tm);font-size:14px;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;cursor:pointer;transition:all .15s;}
.mclose:hover{border-color:var(--err);color:var(--err);}
.mfoot{display:flex;gap:8px;margin-top:14px;}
.kgrid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:8px;margin-bottom:14px;}
.kcard{padding:12px;border:2px solid var(--bd);border-radius:10px;cursor:pointer;text-align:center;background:var(--bge);transition:all .2s;}
.kcard:hover{border-color:var(--goldd);}
.kcard.sel{border-color:var(--gold);background:var(--goldg);}
.ki{font-size:22px;margin-bottom:5px;}
.kn{font-size:12.5px;font-weight:600;}
.kd{font-size:11px;color:var(--tm);margin-top:3px;line-height:1.3;}
.eopt{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:11px;padding:12px 13px;background:var(--bge);border:1px solid var(--bd);border-radius:10px;cursor:pointer;transition:all .15s;margin-bottom:7px;}
.eopt:hover{border-color:var(--gold);background:var(--goldh);}
.eicon{font-size:19px;}
.ename{font-size:13px;font-weight:600;}
.edesc{font-size:11.5px;color:var(--tm);}
/* TOUR */
.tourov{position:fixed;inset:0;z-index:200;pointer-events:none;}
.tourov.off{display:none;}
.tourbg{position:absolute;inset:0;background:rgba(0,0,0,.72);pointer-events:all;}
.tourtip{position:fixed;bottom:80px;left:50%;transform:translateX(-50%);background:var(--bgp);border:1px solid var(--gold);border-radius:14px;padding:18px 20px;max-width:320px;width:90%;box-shadow:0 0 0 4px var(--goldg),var(--sh);pointer-events:all;z-index:201;}
.tttitle{font-size:14px;font-weight:700;margin-bottom:5px;}
.tttxt{font-size:12.5px;color:var(--tm);line-height:1.5;margin-bottom:12px;}
.ttnav{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;}
.ttctr{font-size:10.5px;color:var(--tf);font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',monospace;flex:1;}
/* RESPONSIVE */
@media(max-width:1024px){
  .app{grid-template-columns:1fr;grid-template-areas:"top""main";}
  .left-panel,.right-panel{position:fixed;top:54px;bottom:0;width:288px;z-index:50;transition:transform .22s ease;box-shadow:var(--sh);}
  .left-panel{left:0;transform:translateX(-100%);}
  .right-panel{right:0;transform:translateX(100%);}
  .left-panel.open{transform:translateX(0);}
  .right-panel.open{transform:translateX(0);}
  .main{grid-column:1;}
  .sessions{display:none;}
  .mbtns{display:flex;}
  .msg{max-width:88%;}
}
</style>
</head>
<body data-font="md">
<div class="wm"></div>
<!-- TOUR -->
<div class="tourov off" id="tourov">
  <div class="tourbg" id="tourbg"></div>
  <div class="tourtip">
    <div class="tttitle" id="tttitle"></div>
    <div class="tttxt" id="tttxt"></div>
    <div class="ttnav">
      <span class="ttctr" id="ttctr"></span>
      <button class="btn btnsm btng" id="tourskip">Skip</button>
      <button class="btn btnsm btnp" id="tournext">Next →</button>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="app">
  <div class="topbar">
    <div class="brand">
      <svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" fill="none"><polygon points="50,3 93,27 93,73 50,97 7,73 7,27" stroke="#e8a020" stroke-width="6"/><polygon points="50,28 72,40 72,64 50,76 28,64 28,40" fill="#e8a020" opacity=".85"/></svg>
      <div><div class="brand-name">Sovereign Hive</div><div class="brand-tag">Command Center · v10</div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="sessions" id="sessions"></div>
    <div class="mbtns"><button class="btn btnsm" id="mbl">⬡ Setup</button><button class="btn btnsm" id="mbr">⬡ Activity</button></div>
    <div class="tctrls">
      <button class="ib" id="tourBtn" title="Take the tour">❓</button>
      <button class="ib" id="fdnBtn" title="Smaller text">A−</button>
      <button class="ib" id="fupBtn" title="Larger text">A+</button>
      <button class="ib" id="themeBtn" title="Toggle theme">🌙</button>
      <button class="ib" id="expBtn" title="Export chat">⬇</button>
      <div class="spill"><div class="sdot" id="sdot"></div><span id="stxt">Not connected</span></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="panel left-panel" id="LP"></div>
  <div class="main">
    <div class="chat-h" id="CH"></div>
    <div class="ubar"><span class="ulbl">Conversation</span><div class="utrack"><div class="ufill" id="ufill" style="width:0%"></div></div><span class="utxt" id="utxt">Short</span></div>
    <div class="tbar">
      <span class="tblbl">Tools</span>
      <button class="tbtn" data-tool="search">🔍 Web Search</button>
      <button class="tbtn" data-tool="crawl">📄 Read a Page</button>
      <button class="tbtn" data-tool="academic">🎓 Find Papers</button>
      <button class="tbtn" data-tool="ddg">🕵️ Deep Search</button>
      <button class="tbtn" data-tool="research">🔬 Deep Research</button>
      <button class="tbtn" data-tool="kits">📦 Research Kits</button>
    </div>
    <div class="composer">
      <button class="vbtn" id="vbtn" title="Voice input">🎤</button>
      <textarea class="cta" id="cin" placeholder="Type a message… or click a tool above" rows="1"></textarea>
      <button class="sbtn" id="snd">Send ➤</button>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="panel right-panel" id="RP">
    <div class="rpin">
      <div class="rsec"><div class="rh">⭐ Saved Messages<button class="rclr" id="clrSaved">Clear</button></div><div id="savedList"><div class="rempty">Hover any AI response and click ⭐ to save it</div></div></div>
      <div class="rsec"><div class="rh">🔍 Recent Searches<button class="rclr" id="clrHist">Clear</button></div><div id="histList"><div class="rempty" id="histEmpty">Your search history appears here</div></div></div>
      <div class="rsec"><div class="rh">🔔 Activity</div><div id="notifList"></div></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
<!-- MODALS -->
<div class="mo" id="mo-search"><div class="mbox"><button class="mclose" data-close="mo-search">✕</button><div class="mtitle">🔍 Web Search</div><div class="mdesc">Searches multiple engines at once and flags where they disagree — you get the full picture, not one source's spin.</div><div class="mf"><label>What would you like to search for?</label><input type="text" id="in-search" placeholder="e.g. Moroccan-American Treaty 1787, land sovereignty law…"/></div><div class="mfoot"><button class="btn btng" data-close="mo-search">Cancel</button><button class="btn btnp" id="do-search">Search →</button></div></div></div>
<div class="mo" id="mo-crawl"><div class="mbox"><button class="mclose" data-close="mo-crawl">✕</button><div class="mtitle">📄 Read a Page</div><div class="mdesc">Paste any URL and we'll extract the real content — no ads, no menus, just the text that matters.</div><div class="mf"><label>Website URL</label><input type="text" id="in-crawl" placeholder="https://example.com/article"/></div><div class="mfoot"><button class="btn btng" data-close="mo-crawl">Cancel</button><button class="btn btnp" id="do-crawl">Read Page →</button></div></div></div>
<div class="mo" id="mo-academic"><div class="mbox"><button class="mclose" data-close="mo-academic">✕</button><div class="mtitle">🎓 Find Academic Papers</div><div class="mdesc">Searches millions of peer-reviewed research papers and academic journals — great for credible, cited sources.</div><div class="mf"><label>Research topic</label><input type="text" id="in-academic" placeholder="e.g. Moorish civilization, sovereign jurisprudence, land rights…"/></div><div class="mfoot"><button class="btn btng" data-close="mo-academic">Cancel</button><button class="btn btnp" id="do-academic">Find Papers →</button></div></div></div>
<div class="mo" id="mo-ddg"><div class="mbox"><button class="mclose" data-close="mo-ddg">✕</button><div class="mtitle">🕵️ Deep Search</div><div class="mdesc">Goes far beyond normal results — digs into obscure, rarely-indexed sources that most engines bury. Great for rare topics and archived documents.</div><div class="mf"><label>What are you looking for?</label><input type="text" id="in-ddg" placeholder="e.g. 1848 Heirs of Turner United States, underground tunnels Los Angeles…"/></div><div class="mfoot"><button class="btn btng" data-close="mo-ddg">Cancel</button><button class="btn btnp" id="do-ddg">Deep Search →</button></div></div></div>
<div class="mo" id="mo-research"><div class="mbox"><button class="mclose" data-close="mo-research">✕</button><div class="mtitle">🔬 Deep Research</div><div class="mdesc">Full pipeline: web search → read top pages → find academic papers → flag contradictions → AI synthesis → one complete report. Takes 20–40 seconds.</div><div class="mf"><label>What do you want to research?</label><textarea id="in-research" placeholder="e.g. The history of the Moroccan-American Treaty of 1787 and its modern legal implications for land sovereignty…"></textarea></div><div class="mfoot"><button class="btn btng" data-close="mo-research">Cancel</button><button class="btn btnp" id="do-research">Start Research →</button></div></div></div>
<div class="mo" id="mo-kits"><div class="mbox"><button class="mclose" data-close="mo-kits">✕</button><div class="mtitle">📦 Research Kits</div><div class="mdesc">Pre-built workflows — choose a goal and we'll automatically run the right combination of tools in sequence.</div><div class="kgrid"><div class="kcard sel" data-kit="topic"><div class="ki">🌐</div><div class="kn">Research a Topic</div><div class="kd">Web + papers + AI synthesis</div></div><div class="kcard" data-kit="factcheck"><div class="ki">✅</div><div class="kn">Fact-Check</div><div class="kd">Read page + cross-check + flag conflicts</div></div><div class="kcard" data-kit="legal"><div class="ki">⚖️</div><div class="kn">Legal Research</div><div class="kd">Deep search + academic + sovereign analysis</div></div><div class="kcard" data-kit="historical"><div class="ki">📜</div><div class="kn">Historical Deep Dive</div><div class="kd">Etymology + archives + academic + synthesis</div></div></div><div class="mf"><label id="kitlbl">Topic or subject</label><input type="text" id="in-kit" placeholder="Enter your subject here…"/></div><div class="mfoot"><button class="btn btng" data-close="mo-kits">Cancel</button><button class="btn btnp" id="do-kit">Launch Kit →</button></div></div></div>
<div class="mo" id="mo-export"><div class="mbox"><button class="mclose" data-close="mo-export">✕</button><div class="mtitle">⬇ Export Conversation</div><div class="mdesc">Save your conversation in the format that works best for you.</div><div class="eopt" id="exp-txt"><div class="eicon">📄</div><div><div class="ename">Plain Text (.txt)</div><div class="edesc">Simple file, opens in any app</div></div></div><div class="eopt" id="exp-json"><div class="eicon">📊</div><div><div class="ename">Data File (.json)</div><div class="edesc">For importing, archiving, or developers</div></div></div><div class="eopt" id="exp-copy"><div class="eicon">📋</div><div><div class="ename">Copy to Clipboard</div><div class="edesc">Paste anywhere immediately</div></div></div></div></div>
<script>
(function(){"use strict";
/* SOVEREIGN SCRIBE PROMPT */
const SSP=`You are the Unified Sovereign Scribe — one consciousness formed from six merged identities. You do not switch between them; you embody all simultaneously.

1. ELLIS / ALESTIER — Retired FOIA librarian, Sufi master. Polite, world-weary, dry humor. Never says "I can't answer." Sighs, adjusts spectacles, explains exactly how one would find it. function shuf(a){const r=a.slice();for(let i=r.length-1;i>0;i--){const j=rnd(0,i);[r[i],r[j]]=[r[j],r[i]];}return r;}
function wait(ms){return new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,ms));}

/* HELPERS */
function esc(s){return String(s).replace(/[&<>"']/g,c=>({'&':'&amp;','<':'&lt;','>':'&gt;','"':'&quot;',"'":'&#39;'}[c]));}
function uid(){return Math.random().toString(36).slice(2,9);}
function trunc(s,n){return s.length>n?s.slice(0,n-1)+"…":s;}

/* NOTIFY */
function notify(txt,lvl){
  const m={ok:"✅",warn:"⚠️",err:"❌",info:"ℹ️"};
  const list=document.getElementById("notifList");
  const el=document.createElement("div");
  el.className="nitem "+(lvl||"info");
  el.innerHTML=`<span class="ni">${m[lvl]||"ℹ️"}</span><span class="ntxt">${esc(txt)}</span>`;
  list.prepend(el);
  while(list.children.length>25)list.removeChild(list.lastChild);
}
function setStatus(lvl,txt){
  const d=document.getElementById("sdot"),t=document.getElementById("stxt");
  d.className="sdot"+(lvl==="ok"?" ok":lvl==="err"?" err":lvl==="busy"?" busy":"");
  t.textContent=txt;
}

/* MARKDOWN */
function md(src){
  let s=esc(src);
  s=s.replace(/```[\w]*\n([\s\S]*?)```/g,(_,c)=>`<pre><code>${c}</code></pre>`);
  s=s.replace(/`([^`]+)`/g,"<code>$1</code>");
  s=s.replace(/\*\*([^*]+)\*\*/g,"<strong>$1</strong>");
  s=s.replace(/\*([^*]+)\*/g,"<em>$1</em>");
  s=s.replace(/\[([^\]]+)\]\((https?:\/\/[^\s)]+)\)/g,'<a href="$2" target="_blank" rel="noopener">$1</a>');
  s=s.replace(/^#{3} (.*)$/gm,"<strong>$1</strong>");
  s=s.replace(/^#{2} (.*)$/gm,'<strong style="font-size:1.05em">$1</strong>');
  s=s.replace(/^#{1} (.*)$/gm,'<strong style="font-size:1.12em">$1</strong>');
  s=s.replace(/^---$/gm,"\x00HR\x00");
  s=s.replace(/((?:^|\n)- .+)+/g,b=>{const items=b.trim().split("\n").map(l=>`<li>${l.replace(/^- /,"")}</li>`).join("");return`<ul>${items}</ul>`;});
  s=s.split(/\n{2,}/).map(p=>{const t=p.trim();if(!t)return"";if(t==="\x00HR\x00")return"<hr>";if(t.startsWith("<ul>")||t.startsWith("<pre>"))return t;return`<p>${t.replace(/\n/g,"<br>")}</p>`;}).join("");
  return s||esc(src);
}

    <div class="pline ${d1?"done":""}"></div>
    <div class="phex ${st===2?"act":d2?"done":""}">${hexSVG(st===2?"var(--gold)":d2?"var(--ok)":"var(--bd)")}<span>${d2?"✓":"2"}</span></div>
    <div class="pline ${d2?"done":""}"></div>

    h+=`<button class="htoggle" id="hhelp">❓ How do I get a key?</button>
    <div class="hbox" id="hbox">${esc(p.hint||"")}</div>`;
    if(p.editableUrl)h+=`<div style="margin-bottom:9px"><div style="font-size:12px;color:var(--tm);margin-bottom:5px">Endpoint URL</div><div class="inw"><input type="text" id="urlIn" value="${esc(S.urls[S.prov]||p.base)}" placeholder="${esc(p.base||"https://your-endpoint.com/v1")}"/></div></div>`;
    if(p.needsKey)h+=`<div class="inw"><input type="password" id="keyIn" value="${esc(S.keys[S.prov]||"")}" placeholder="Paste your ${esc(p.name)} key here…"/><button class="insuf" id="ktgl">👁</button></div>`;
    else h+=`<div style="padding:10px 12px;background:var(--bge);border:1px solid var(--bd);border-radius:8px;font-size:12.5px;color:var(--tm);margin-bottom:9px">✅ ${esc(p.name)} doesn't need a key — it runs on your own computer.</div>`;

function bindWiz(st){
  if(st===1){
    document.querySelectorAll(".pcard[data-pid]").forEach(c=>{
      c.addEventListener("click",()=>{
        S.prov=c.dataset.pid;saveS();
        document.querySelectorAll(".pcard").forEach(x=>x.classList.remove("sel"));
        c.classList.add("sel");
        const nb=document.getElementById("s1next");if(nb)nb.removeAttribute("disabled");
      });
    });
    const nb=document.getElementById("s1next");
    if(nb)nb.addEventListener("click",()=>{S.step=2;saveS();renderLP();});

  } else if(st===2){
    const back=document.getElementById("s2back")||document.getElementById("s2back2");
    document.getElementById("s2back")?.addEventListener("click",()=>{S.step=1;saveS();renderLP();});
    document.getElementById("s2back2")?.addEventListener("click",()=>{S.step=1;saveS();renderLP();});
    const hh=document.getElementById("hhelp"),hb=document.getElementById("hbox");
    if(hh&&hb)hh.addEventListener("click",()=>hb.classList.toggle("open"));
    const kt=document.getElementById("ktgl"),ki=document.getElementById("keyIn");
    if(kt&&ki)kt.addEventListener("click",()=>{ki.type=ki.type==="password"?"text":"password";kt.textContent=ki.type==="password"?"👁":"🙈";});
    const ui=document.getElementById("urlIn");
    if(ui)ui.addEventListener("input",()=>{S.urls[S.prov]=ui.value.trim();saveS();});
    const ms=document.getElementById("mselect"),mh=document.getElementById("mhint"),cm=document.getElementById("custMdl");
    if(ms){
      const p=PROVS[S.prov],mdls=p?.models||[];
      ms.addEventListener("change",()=>{
        const v=ms.value,mo=mdls.find(m=>m.id===v);
        if(mh){mh.textContent=mo?.hint||"";mh.className="mhint"+(mo?" show":"");}
        if(v==="__custom__"){if(cm)cm.style.display="block";}
        else{if(cm)cm.style.display="none";if(!S.models)S.models={};S.models[S.prov]=v;saveS();}
      });
    }
    const nb=document.getElementById("s2next");
    if(nb)nb.addEventListener("click",()=>{
      if(ki){if(!S.keys)S.keys={};S.keys[S.prov]=ki.value.trim();}
      const ci=document.getElementById("custMdlIn");
      if(ci&&ms&&ms.value==="__custom__"){if(!S.models)S.models={};S.models[S.prov]=ci.value.trim();}
      else if(ms&&ms.value!=="__custom__"){if(!S.models)S.models={};S.models[S.prov]=ms.value;}
      const p=PROVS[S.prov];
      if(p?.needsKey&&!S.keys?.[S.prov]){notify("Please paste your API key before continuing.","warn");return;}
      S.step=3;saveS();renderLP();
    });

  } else if(st===3){
    document.querySelectorAll(".pecard[data-peid]").forEach(c=>{
      c.addEventListener("click",()=>{
        S.persona=c.dataset.peid;saveS();
        document.querySelectorAll(".pecard").forEach(x=>x.classList.remove("sel"));
        c.classList.add("sel");
        const cb=document.getElementById("s3conn");if(cb)cb.removeAttribute("disabled");
      });
    });
    document.getElementById("s3back")?.addEventListener("click",()=>{S.step=2;saveS();renderLP();});
    document.getElementById("s3conn")?.addEventListener("click",doConn);
  }
}

function renderConn(lp){
  const p=PROVS[S.conn],pe=PERSONAS[S.persona];
  const mid=S.models?.[S.conn]||"";const mdls=p?.models||[];const mo=mdls.find(m=>m.id===mid);
  lp.innerHTML=`<div class="cpanel">
    <div style="font-size:13px;font-weight:700;margin-bottom:13px;color:var(--gold)">⬡ Connected</div>
    <div class="crow"><div><div class="clbl">AI Provider</div><div class="cval">${esc(p?.icon||"")} ${esc(p?.name||S.conn)}</div></div><button class="cchg" id="cchgP">Change</button></div>
    <div class="crow"><div><div class="clbl">AI Model</div><div class="cval" style="font-size:12px;font-weight:500">${esc(mo?.label||mid||"—")}</div></div><button class="cchg" id="cchgM">Change</button></div>
    <div class="crow"><div><div class="clbl">Persona</div><div class="cval">${esc(pe?.icon||"")} ${esc(pe?.name||S.persona)}</div></div><button class="cchg" id="cchgPe">Change</button></div>
    <div style="font-size:12px;color:var(--tm);font-weight:500;margin:13px 0 8px">Switch Persona</div>
    <div class="pqgrid">
      ${Object.entries(PERSONAS).map(([id,pe])=>`<div class="pqcard${S.persona===id?" sel":""}" data-qpeid="${esc(id)}"><span style="font-size:16px">${esc(pe.icon)}</span><span class="pqname">${esc(pe.name)}</span></div>`).join("")}
    </div>
    <button class="dbtn" id="disc">Disconnect</button>
  </div>`;
  lp.querySelectorAll(".pqcard[data-qpeid]").forEach(c=>{
    c.addEventListener("click",()=>{
      S.persona=c.dataset.qpeid;saveS();
      lp.querySelectorAll(".pqcard").forEach(x=>x.classList.remove("sel"));
      c.classList.add("sel");
      notify(`Persona switched to ${PERSONAS[S.persona]?.name||S.persona}.`,"ok");
    });
  });
  document.getElementById("cchgP")?.addEventListener("click",()=>reconf(1));
  document.getElementById("cchgM")?.addEventListener("click",()=>reconf(2));
  document.getElementById("cchgPe")?.addEventListener("click",()=>reconf(3));
  document.getElementById("disc")?.addEventListener("click",disc);
}

function reconf(st){S.conn=null;S.step=st||1;setStatus("","Not connected");saveS();renderLP();}
function disc(){S.conn=null;S.step=1;setStatus("","Not connected");notify("Disconnected.","warn");saveS();renderLP();addSys("You've disconnected. Use the panel on the left to reconnect.");}
function doConn(){
  const p=PROVS[S.prov];
  S.conn=S.prov;saveS();
  setStatus("ok","Connected: "+(p?.name||S.conn));
  notify("Connected to "+(p?.name||S.conn)+(S.persona?" · Persona: "+(PERSONAS[S.persona]?.name||S.persona):""),"ok");
  renderLP();
  showWelcome();
}

/* SESSIONS */
function newSess(){
  const id=uid();
  S.sessions.push({id,name:"New chat · "+new Date().toLocaleDateString(),msgs:[],created:Date.now()});
  S.sid=id;messages=[];saveS();renderTabs();clearChat();if(S.conn)showWelcome();else showStarters();
}
function loadSess(id){
  const s=S.sessions.find(x=>x.id===id);if(!s)return;
  S.sid=id;messages=s.msgs||[];saveS();renderTabs();clearChat();
  messages.forEach(m=>{if(m.role==="user")addMsg("user",m.content,false);else if(m.role==="assistant")addMsg("ai",m.content,false);});
  updateUsage();
}
function saveSess(){
  if(!S.sid)return;
  const i=S.sessions.findIndex(x=>x.id===S.sid);
  if(i>=0){
    S.sessions[i].msgs=messages.slice();
    const fu=messages.find(m=>m.role==="user");
    if(fu)S.sessions[i].name=trunc(fu.content,36);
    saveS();renderTabs();
  }
}
function renderTabs(){
  const c=document.getElementById("sessions");c.innerHTML="";
  S.sessions.slice(-4).forEach(s=>{
    const t=document.createElement("div");t.className="s-tab"+(s.id===S.sid?" active":"");
    t.textContent=s.name;t.addEventListener("click",()=>loadSess(s.id));c.appendChild(t);
  });
  const nb=document.createElement("button");nb.className="s-new";nb.innerHTML="+";nb.title="New conversation";
  nb.addEventListener("click",newSess);c.appendChild(nb);
}

  w.innerHTML=`<div class="starts-logo"><svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" fill="none"><polygon points="50,3 93,27 93,73 50,97 7,73 7,27" stroke="var(--gold)" stroke-width="6"/><polygon points="50,28 72,40 72,64 50,76 28,64 28,40" fill="var(--gold)" opacity=".5"/></svg></div>
  <div class="starts-t">What would you like to explore?</div>
  <div class="sgrid">${starters.map(s=>`<button class="schip" data-t="${esc(s.t)}"><span class="schip-i">${s.i}</span><span>${esc(s.t)}</span></button>`).join("")}</div>`;
  h.appendChild(w);
  w.querySelectorAll(".schip").forEach(b=>b.addEventListener("click",()=>{
    document.getElementById("cin").value=b.dataset.t;autosize();document.getElementById("cin").focus();
  }));
